title: Cohort Manifest
description: Schema for a cohort-manifest document per design C12. A cohort is a named, downstream-consumable grouping of catalog members (skills, agents, commands, rules, hooks) drawn from the closed cohort set (core, developer, security, research, ai-engineering, full). The manifest carries a per_harness_targets contract that lets a consumer resolve, for each cohort and harness, the native plugin target WITHOUT re-deriving the mapping: it references the propagation manifest as the single source of truth. Exhaustive membership population is owned by a later phase; this schema fixes the SHAPE.

version.description: SemVer version of the cohort manifest.

cohorts.description: The cohort entries declared by this manifest.

per_harness_targets.description: Contract describing how a downstream consumer resolves each cohort's per-harness native plugin target. References the propagation manifest as the source of truth rather than restating the mapping.

description.description: What the cohort provides and who it targets.

members.description: Member names grouped by catalog item type. Each list holds stable kebab-case member identifiers.

items.description: Stable kebab-case member identifier corresponding to an artifact under src/apothem/.

source.description: Relative path (from src/apothem/) to the propagation manifest that is the single source of truth for per-harness native targets. A consumer resolves a cohort member's native plugin target by looking up the member's catalog item type in this manifest's `harnesses.<harness>.install` list.

harnesses.description: The closed harness cohort whose native targets are resolvable through the source manifest.

resolution.description: Human-readable note describing the resolution rule: for a given cohort member of catalog type T and a target harness H, the native plugin target is the `target` field of the entry in propagation-manifest.yaml `harnesses.H.install` whose `source` matches `T/` (e.g. `skills/`, `agents/`, `commands/`, `rules/`, `hooks/`).
